measured: Application calls and optional settings are recorded below at the cited commits.

applications.name: volter-ai/runhuman-2 (RH2)
applications.client: fetch in the RH2 Slack app's worker (JSON bodies, Bearer bot token) and the channel bridge's worker (form bodies, Bearer bot token); oauth.v2.access as a form with the client credentials

backend.call: the install's code exchanged for the workspace's bot token
the task's root message, its thread replies and the status message
the status message updated in place
a public channel the app is not in is joined after not_in_channel
a note to the person alone in the thread
the bridge's install: its code exchanged for the workspace's bot token
the bridge finds the installed workspace that can see a linked channel
a Conversation's line posted in its channel under its author's name (username, unfurl_links false)
a person's name for a line the bridge carries into RH2

frontend.call: Slack OAuth consent (commands, chat:write, channels:history, channels:join, groups:history, im:history)

webhooks.receives: a signed slash command, answered in its acknowledgement's body with a reply to the person alone (link, config, help) or acknowledged empty while the task runs
a signed message event (a person's reply in a task thread) and url_verification
the bridge's signed message event (a person's line in a linked channel) and url_verification

applications.name: volter-ai/supercode (Volter Harness)
applications.client: the Chat SDK's Slack adapter in Socket Mode (chat@4.39.0, @chat-adapter/slack 4.39.0 over @slack/web-api 7.18.0 and @slack/socket-mode 2.0.5), SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_APP_TOKEN from Hermes's .env (chat-sdk.mjs:79); configuration read at sdk/orchestrator/adapters/chat-sdk.mjs:10,79,209-211

backend.call: the adapter's initialize reads the bot's own user and bot id
Socket Mode: the app-level token asks where to connect
Socket Mode's connection: events_api envelopes (a message in a channel or a DM, an app_mention), each acknowledged by its envelope_id
a message's author named for the inbound turn
the agent's reply posted in the thread (text, thread_ts, unfurl_links and unfurl_media false)
a reply's files uploaded into the thread (files.uploadV2: the upload URL asked, the bytes posted to it, the upload completed with channel_id and thread_ts)
the reply that carries files, its text as markdown_text

applications.name: Twin (twin-world's own callers)
applications.client: the on-call recipe's @slack/web-api WebClient (cookbook/on-call-agent, an executed page whose app is Slack's official SDK unmodified) with the World's SLACK_BOT_TOKEN

backend.call: the agent finds #ops
the agent posts the ticket it filed
the recipe reads the notification back from the channel's history

applications.client: fetch with the bot token (Bearer); SLACK_ID and SLACK_SECRET in the token exchange's form

backend.call: the channel's code exchanged for the bot token
the bot's user, read by GET with its id in the query, for the channel's name and picture
the channels a post can go to, by GET with types=public_channel,private_channel
the bot joins the post's channel first
the post, and a comment in its thread, as blocks under the channel's username and icon_url
the post's permalink, by GET

frontend.call: Slack OAuth consent (channels:read, chat:write, users:read, groups:read, channels:join, chat:write.customize)

applications.name: gitroomhq/postiz-app
dubinc/dub (Dub)

backend.call: Create shared support channel
Read support group membership
Invite support group to channel
Invite customer through Slack Connect
Mirror support chat

applications.gate: Priority support calls Slack using the supplied bot credential (apps/web/lib/slack/client.ts:7-13; apps/web/lib/slack/support-invite.ts:27,40,82,115; apps/web/app/api/ai/support-chat/route.ts:257).

optional.what: Dub's operations log (alerts, cron, errors, links, payouts) posted to its team's incoming webhooks
optional.setting: Configuration: operator instrumentation is a setting that turns the reporting provider on; operator-only log shipping defaults to console, skips outside VERCEL_ENV=production, and skips an absent hook; no customer uses this stream (packages/utils/src/functions/log.ts:18-27).

optional.what: the Slack app (an assistant answering mentions, and workflow steps that post, update or delete messages, send ephemerals, add reactions and list channels), @slack/web-api
optional.setting: Install (2): install the Slack application in the workspace before connecting it; it is a marketplace application, not the standard workspace application (packages/twenty-apps/public/slack/src/application.config.ts:1-15; packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/application/application-marketplace/constants/marketplace-vetted-applications.constant.ts:30). Workspace creation installs only the standard application (packages/twenty-server/src/engine/workspace-manager/workspace-manager.service.ts:64-68); Slack is a separate marketplace package.

optional.client: fetch (form bodies), SLACK_CLIENT_ID and SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET in the token exchange's body; its webhooks to the install's incoming webhook URL are delivered by QStash

backend.call: the install's code exchanged for the bot token and the incoming webhook
the person who ran /shorten, by their profile's email
the integration removed in Dub: the app uninstalled with the bot token and the client credentials
Dub's events (a link made, a click, a lead, a sale) posted as blocks to the install's incoming webhook

frontend.call: Slack OAuth consent (chat:write, commands, im:write, channels:join, chat:write.customize, links:write, users.profile:read, users:read.email, users:read, incoming-webhook)

webhooks.receives: a signed /shorten slash command, answered in its acknowledgement's body with blocks

optional.what: Workspace Slack app installation and command/event forwarding
optional.setting: Install (2): the workspace installs the Slack integration before commands and forwarding; no default installedIntegration (apps/web/app/api/slack/callback/route.ts:76-90; apps/web/lib/integrations/slack/oauth.ts:14,42-47).
